Variable degree of defects in exit from naïve pluripotency in NMD-deficient ESCs

To delineate the molecular function of NMD in the exit from naïve pluripotency, we generated Rex1-33 GFPd2 reporter ESC lines 4, 23 deficient for the three NMD downstream effectors Smg5, Smg6 or Smg7 34 (NMD KO ESCs), and corresponding rescue cell lines in which the missing NMD-factor was re-expressed 35 (NMD rescue ESCs) (Extended Data Fig. 1a,b). NMD KO cells showed normal ESC morphology, cell cycle 36 profile and telomere maintenance (Extended Data Fig. 1c,d), but exhibited pronounced delays in the exit 37 from naïve pluripotency. This manifested in delayed downregulation of the Rex1-GFPd2 reporter 24 h 38 after the onset of differentiation (N24) and delayed entry into commitment, assayed 72 h after 2i 39 withdrawal (Fig. 1a,b). Both defects were restored in rescue cell lines, showing causality of NMD-factor 40 deficiency for delays in exit from naïve pluripotency (Fig 1a,b). The three NMD-factor KOs displayed 41 variable degrees of differentiation delays: the strongest effect was observed in the absence of Smg5 and 42 the weakest in the absence of Smg7. This does not align with the proposed strictly heterodimer-43 dependent function of Smg5 and Smg7, which would predict similar phenotypes for Smg5 and Smg7 KOs 44 [24][25][26] . The results therefore suggest a less strict heterodimer dependence than anticipated for the activity 45 of either Smg5 or Smg7. 46 followed the same trend as the differentiation phenotype and deregulation of the NMD target Gadd45b 93 (pUpf1 levels in Smg5 KO > Smg6 KO > Smg7 KO > WT ESCs). Upf1 is phosphorylated by the kinase Smg1 94 27,28 . Smg1 mRNA is itself an NMD target, but in contrast to pUpf1 is upregulated to a similar extent in all 95 three NMD KO ESCs (Extended Data Fig. 2a). Therefore, graded increase of pUpf1 levels in NMD KOs is 96 unlikely to be a direct effect of higher Smg1 expression. Impaired Upf1 dephosphorylation may therefore 97 underlie increased pUpf1 levels in NMD mutant cells. The three NMD effectors Smg5, Smg6 and Smg7 98 have all been implicated in the recruitment of PP2A to dephosphorylate Upf1 25, 26 , but the strongest 99 increase of pUpf1 in Smg5 KO ESCs suggests that Smg5 acts as the main PP2A recruiter during NMD 100 (Extended Data Fig. 2b).

Eif4a2 is a bona-fide NMD target in ESCs and its NMD sensitivity is evolutionarily conserved

Among the 57 NMD targets with potential phenotypic relevance, our attention was drawn to the RNA 187 helicase Eif4a2, a component of the Eif4F translation initiation complex, which mediates 5' cap recognition 188 by the small ribosomal subunit 30, 31 . Several layers of evidence suggest Eif4a2 as a bona-fide NMD target.

Firstly, the Eif4a2 locus encodes for two splice-isoforms: one full-length protein, and one PTC-containing 190 isoform (Fig. 4a). Secondly, Eif4a2 mRNA levels were significantly increased after translation inhibition by 191 cycloheximide (CHX) treatment, a hallmark of bona-fide NMD targets (Fig. 4b) (Fig. 4c). Full length Eif4a2 (Eif4a2 FL ) protein levels were increased in NMD KO cells (Fig. 4d). The

Eif4a2 PTC isoform produced a protein that was weakly detected by western blot analysis in WT and NMD  Table S3), nor did they 202 react to CHX treatment (Extended Data Fig. 4d). Taken together, this identifies Eif4a2 as a bona-fide NMD 203 target in ESCs and shows that NMD disruption leads to the production of an Eif4a2 PTC protein.

The linkage of NMD to Eif4a2 expression appears to be conserved in evolution. The gene structure of 205 Eif4a2 is strikingly similar between mouse, dog and human (Fig. 4e). The mouse Eif4a2 coding sequence 206 showed identities of 94%, 95% and 98.5% to human, dog and rat, respectively (Fig. 4f). Despite the PTC-207 exon being under no apparent selective pressure to maintain protein-coding potential (PTC at nucleotide 208 position 8 out of 107 in this exon), we observed 96.4%, 98.2% and 99% nucleotide identity for human, dog and rat, respectively, on par with the other well conserved Eif4a2 exons. Conservation of UTRs and introns 210 was significantly lower (Fig. 4f). In a transcriptome-wide comparison, the Eif4a2 PTC exon showed high 211 conservation at the nucleotide level: less than 5% of all exons and less than 3% of all UTRs showed higher 212 conservation rates between mouse and rat than the Eif4a2 PTC exon ( Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 4e-g).
In the comparisons with human and dog these percentages were even lower. Therefore, the potential of 214 Eif4a2 to be regulated by NMD is a feature conserved in mammalian evolution.
Eif4a2 is causative for defects in exit from naïve pluripotency in NMD-deficient ESCs

To delineate a potential causative relationship between increased Eif4a2 levels and the differentiation 218 defect observed in NMD-deficient cells, we generated Eif4a2 KO cells and NMD (Smg5 or Smg6) / Eif4a2 219 double deficient cells (collectively referred to as NMD/Eif4a2 dKO) by deleting all potential Eif4a2 isoforms 220 or specifically Eif4a2 PTC (Fig. 5a and Extended Data Fig. 5a). All Eif4a2 KO cell lines proliferated normally, 221 showed normal ESC morphology and could be maintained for more than 10 passages. Deletion of the PTC 222 exon resulted in an increase in full length Eif4a2 protein levels in WT and NMD KO ESCs (Fig. 5a). Both the 223 complete absence of Eif4a2 or specific deletion of Eif4a2 PTC accelerated Rex1-GFPd2 downregulation 224 kinetics in WT cells (Fig. 5b), suggesting that increased expression of Eif4a2 PTC and not full-length Eif4a2 is 225 the major cause of the differentiation block. In NMD/Eif4a2 FL and NMD/Eif4a2 PTC dKO cells, differentiation 226 kinetics were substantially rescued in a Rex1-GFPd2 assay (Fig. 5b). Accordingly, Klf4 and Nanog 227 expression levels were downregulated to near WT-levels at N30 (Fig. 5c). Similar effects were observed 228 for protein levels of the naïve TFs Nanog and Esrrb at N24 (Extended Data Fig. 5b). Phenotypic rescue in 229 NMD/Eif4a2 PTC double KO cells, in which Eif4a2 FL protein levels are even further increased, supports the 230 proposition that Eif4a2 PTC is the major mediator of the observed defect in exit from naïve pluripotency.

To assess the specificity of Eif4a2 depletion in restoring differentiation potential in an NMD-deficient ESC 232 background, we compared differentiation potential between Tcf7l1 KO and Eif4a2/Tcf7l1 dKO ESCs. Basal leaky expression of differentiation-associated transcripts was reduced 326 already in 2i. Consistently, NMD depletion leads to increased similarities between ESCs and the naïve in 327 vivo epiblast 6 . Therefore, NMD acts already in self-renewal conditions to prune the differentiation 328 programme. Despite exhibiting delayed downregulation of the pluripotency TF-network, NMD KO EBs 329 eventually initiate formative and primed expression programmes. However, subsequent downregulation 330 of key markers of these states, normally observed around d4 to d6 of EB differentiation, does not occur. 331 This suggests a general role for NMD in dynamically shaping and fine-tuning transcript abundance to 332 facilitate rapid gene regulatory network remodeling during cell fate decisions. 333 Differentiation defects across Smg5, Smg6 and Smg7 KOs scale with deregulation of known NMD target 334 genes and levels of phospho-Upf1, suggesting that NMD defects directly translate to differentiation 335 delays. The striking difference in NMD target regulation and extent of differentiation delays between 336 Smg5 and Smg7 KOs (Smg5 >> Smg7) together with the strong synergistic effects after co-depletion are 337 difficult to reconcile with the proposed obligatory heterodimer dependence of these two factors 24, 26 . We 338 show that a division of labor between Smg5 and Smg7 is causative for the different effects of depletion in 339 the respective KOs. Smg factors have a dual role in triggering RNA degradation and in mediating Upf1 340 dephosphorylation; pUpf1 increase in all three Smg KOs accords with such a role of Smg factors in PP2A 341 recruitment 25, 26 . Our data suggest that Smg7 acts as the main adapter or recruiter for pUpf1. However, 342 by itself it is unable to efficiently dephosphorylate Upf1, as evidenced by high pUpf1 levels in Smg5 KO 343 ESCs, where Smg7 binding to pUpf1 is unaffected. We propose that Smg7 binding to Upf1 without 344 subsequent Upf1 dephosphorylation results in jamming of the dephosphorylation cycle, and ensuing 345 stalling of the mRNA degradation circuit. Aberrant recruitment of Smg6 to mRNA targets already bound 346 by Smg7 and pUpf1 cannot properly restore NMD function in Smg5 KOs. Smg5 alone is unable to bind 347 pUpf1 in our assays. This suggests that the main role of Smg5 lies in its dephosphorylation activity, but recruitment to its substrate is Smg7-dependent. This is consistent with the strongest increase of pUpf1 349 levels and consequently the strongest differentiation delays in Smg5 KO ESCs. 350 Absence of Smg6 causes a strong differentiation delay. This suggests that the exonucleolytic pathway 351 cannot completely compensate for loss of the endonucleolytic activity in Smg6 KOs. Smg7 KO leads to 352 very weak phenotypes and low levels of NMD deregulation. Our data support a model in which, in the 353 absence of Smg7, Smg5 cannot be recruited to pUpf1-bound mRNAs, enabling Smg6 to recognize these 354 potential targets and initiate their degradation. Thereby Smg6 can largely compensate for loss of Smg7, 355 resulting in only mild NMD defects in Smg7 KO cells. However, Smg6 is unable to compensate for the 356 complete absence of the exonucleolytic branch of NMD, suggested by the apparent loss of viability in a 357 Smg5/7 dKO situation. This indicates a function of Smg5 and/or Smg7 in the endonucleolytic decay 358 pathway. Our data are consistent with a function of Smg5 or Smg7 in Upf1 dephosphorylation, which is a 359 key step also in the endonucleolytic Smg6-mediated mRNA decay axis. Despite the weak defects in single 360 Smg7 KO cells, facultative essentiality for Smg7 is revealed in the absence of either Smg5 or Smg6. 361 Accordingly, only Smg5/Smg6 dKO ESCs could be established, showing that Smg7 is sufficient to sustain 362 minimal NMD activity required for survival. This suggests that Smg7 can either interact with potentially 363 novel interactors in the absence of its normal interaction partners, or that Smg7 acts as a jack of all trades, 364 fulfilling minimal roles in target recognition, recruitment of the degradation machinery and Upf1 365 dephosphorylation. Taken together, the mode of action described above explains both the graded pUpf1 366 levels as well as graded impact on NMD of Smg5, Smg6 and Smg7 KOs. 367 A combination of RNA-seq and SLAM-seq based half-life analyses allowed us to compile a list of high-368 confidence NMD targets during the exit from pluripotency. However, while target mRNA identity appears identical, the amplitude of mRNA deregulation scales with both the phenotype and Eif4a2.
